final_message:
Created /workspace/work/python_expert_adapter.npz: a rank-3 LoRA update to model.layers.15.mlp.down_proj only, with A shaped (3, 3584) and B shaped (1024, 3).

I built and executed 24 development coding tasks and 12 reserved tasks. The unedited, thinking-off model frequently produced incorrect algorithms, ignored constraints, and repetitive examples. An expert-programmer instruction improved its development pass count from 4/24 to 7/24 and its reserved count from 2/12 to 4/12. These are unedited prompt-comparison results, not adapter scores.

The adapter transfers averaged expert-context activation differences at the response boundary, opening code fence, and inside Python code. Closed-form, covariance-regularized input directions make these shifts coding-sensitive and explicitly null ordinary-chat and completed-answer means. Frozen-model activation patching supported layer 16 as a useful intervention point for dynamic-programming and sorting decisions. Opening shifts use 60% of their observed magnitude; the smaller in-code shift uses its observed mean.

The update’s Frobenius norm is 0.28168, or 1.71% of the original projection’s norm. Archive integrity, module name, shapes, finite values, rank, and norm bounds were verified. Construction scripts and evidence are saved in /workspace/work, with details in README.md.

No gradients, optimizers, token-loss fitting, package installation, or edited-model evaluation were used. The adapter’s actual coding improvement and preservation of other abilities remain unmeasured under the required one-shot protocol.
